question:
A data table is represented by the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & -1 & 4\\2 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$. During a classroom investigation, the rows and columns of the table are interchanged to form $A^T$. The students then double every entry of the original matrix to form $C=2A$. They examine how transposition and multiplication of the entire matrix by a scalar affect its determinant.

(a) Evaluate $|A|$.

(b) Write the matrix $A^T$.

(c) Evaluate $|A^T|$ and compare it with $|A|$.

(d) Determine $|C|$ without directly expanding $C$ and justify the result.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 4\\1 & 0\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}0 & 4\\2 & 0\end{vmatrix}+3\begin{vmatrix}0 & -1\\2 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=1(0-4)-2(0-8)+3(0+2)$$
$$|A|=-4+16+6=18$$

(b)
Interchanging the rows and columns gives
$$A^T=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2\\2 & -1 & 1\\3 & 4 & 0\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
Expanding $|A^T|$ along the first row,
$$|A^T|=1\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 1\\4 & 0\end{vmatrix}+2\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & 4\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A^T|=-4+2(8+3)=18$$
Thus,
$$|A^T|=|A|=18$$
This verifies that transposition does not change the value of a determinant.

(d)
Since $A$ is a matrix of order $3$, multiplying every entry by $2$ is equivalent to taking $2$ common from each of its three rows. Therefore,
$$|C|=|2A|=2^3|A|$$
$$|C|=8(18)=144$$
Hence, $|C|=144$.
